discovery: Spherical-aberration correction in electron optics, enabling sub-angstrom resolution transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Technische Universität Darmstadt / Ulm University, Germany

nominees.name: Knut Urban
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich / RWTH Aachen University, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics: electron optics and microscopy
motivation: For half a century, Scherzer's theorem held that round electron lenses have unavoidable spherical aberration, which limited TEM resolution far above the electron wavelength. Rose designed a hexapole corrector that overcomes this limit. In 1997–98, Haider built it and Urban demonstrated it, giving the first aberration-corrected TEM with resolution below the interatomic spacing. Correctors are now standard on high-end instruments worldwide. They let us image single atoms, light elements such as oxygen and lithium, interfaces, dislocation cores and dopants. They also allow quantitative mapping of chemistry and bonding column by column. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy has become a routine physical measurement that underpins research on alloys, semiconductors, batteries, catalysts and quantum materials. This is a fundamental advance in physical instrumentation, rigorous in conception and transformative in reach. Its impact matches that of the scanning tunnelling microscope and cryo-electron microscopy, both already recognised by the Nobel Prize.
